title: NVIDIA ForceP2P driver override on a Jarvis AI 2xGPU VM: measured, and it is worth 7-22% of real decode

host.gpus: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 97,887 MiB each, driver 595.58.03
host.topology: nvidia-smi topo -m reports PHB (same PCIe host bridge, single NUMA, CPU affinity 0-55 both) - NOT the NODE case the source doc names, so this is a datapoint the doc did not cover

what_was_already_correct_before_touching.uvm_disable_hmm: Y - the doc's other critical fix was already active on the image
what_was_already_correct_before_touching.BAR1: 131,072 MiB per GPU, larger than the 97,887 MiB of VRAM, so the crippled-256MB BAR case does not apply
what_was_already_correct_before_touching.filesystem: ext4, as the doc recommends over ZFS

what_was_missing.RegistryDwords: empty - the ForceP2P override was not set

change_applied.reload: stop every GPU user first - the vLLM container AND nvidia-dcgm's nv-hostengine both pin nvidia_uvm; docker rm -f the container, systemctl stop nvidia-dcgm, then modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia && modprobe nvidia && modprobe nvidia_uvm
change_applied.verified_runtime: RegistryDwords now reports the full string; EnableResizableBar 1, GrdmaPciTopoCheckOverride 1, DmaRemapPeerMmio 1 - matching the doc's expected signal exactly

p2p_capability_ab.method: same container image, same script, 64 MiB and 256 B cross-device torch copies, 20 and 2000 iterations
p2p_capability_ab.how_to_read_the_latency_number: 8.34 us is an end-to-end torch copy_ including kernel launch and sync, NOT the doc's 0.36-0.45 us P2P write latency from p2pBandwidthLatencyTest. The two are different quantities and must not be differenced. The 12.48 us BEFORE figure does sit in the doc's 'P2P disabled ~14 us' band, which is what identified the fault.
p2p_capability_ab.bandwidth_in_context: 51.98 GB/s is ~93% of the doc's ~54-56 GB/s same-NUMA bare-metal band, achieved inside a passthrough VM

what_it_did_NOT_fix.symm_mem_communicator: vLLM still logs 'SymmMemCommunicator: native P2P atomics are not supported between devices [0, 1], communicator is not available.' P2P memory access and native P2P atomics are separate capabilities; the override enables the former, not the latter, so vLLM's symmetric-memory all-reduce path stays unavailable. The measured gains below therefore come from the ordinary P2P data path, and there may be more left on the table for a host that also has atomics.

decode_ab_on_tp2.config: identical sr1 image, TP=2, shipping depth schedule [[1,4,3],[5,64,1]], 262,144 window, seed 46, same shapes and rungs; only the driver's P2P state differs
decode_ab_on_tp2.fidelity: five-check gate PASS on both arms, including the 262,144-token needle

why_this_mattered_beyond_the_percentages: Measured BEFORE the override, TP2 looked like a bad trade: +11% single-stream over one card and zero aggregate benefit, i.e. a whole second GPU spent on latency alone. With P2P enabled TP2 beats the single card on BOTH axes (+18.4% single-stream and +11.4% C8 aggregate on 512x256, +36.8% single-stream on 4kx1k). Publishing the pre-override numbers as a TP-versus-DP verdict would have recorded a conclusion about this VM's driver configuration as though it were a property of tensor parallelism or of EXL3.

not_applicable_in_a_guest.grub_pcie_aspm_off_pcie_port_pm_off: PCIe link power management lives on host root ports; the guest cmdline cannot reach them (ours is a bare cloud-image cmdline with no PCIe parameters)
not_applicable_in_a_guest.iommu_off: passthrough requires the HOST IOMMU; disabling it in the guest is not the same knob and was not attempted
not_applicable_in_a_guest.bios_resizable_bar_above_4g_sriov: host firmware, not reachable from the VM - and BAR1 already arrives at 128 GiB
not_applicable_in_a_guest.NCCL_P2P_LEVEL_SYS: aimed at cross-NUMA; both GPUs report NUMA 0 with identical CPU affinity, so there is no cross-NUMA hop to bridge here

action_for_every_future_jarvis_multi_gpu: Write the modprobe override and reload the driver BEFORE the first measurement, then verify /proc/driver/nvidia/params and can_device_access_peer. On this host it is worth 7-22% of decode throughput and costs one file plus a driver reload.
